evaluator_independence.description: Independence is a condition at a moment, not a permanent property. Two parties independent when an evaluation ran may later enter a funding, employment, advisory, reciprocal-review, code-contribution or commercial relationship. That later relationship does not falsify the historical fact that the evaluation occurred under the earlier conditions, but it does change how the evaluation should be represented now. Recording only one of the two makes independence either falsely permanent or retroactively erased. Both are recorded.

assessed_at.description: When independence was assessed. This is the date the historical fact attaches to.

independent_at_assessment.description: Whether the evaluator met the independence test in EVIDENCE-MODEL.md at assessed_at. This value is historical and is never edited; a later relationship creates a new current_status, it does not rewrite this.

current_status.description: Standing now. UNCHANGED: re-checked, no qualifying relationship has formed. RELATIONSHIP_FORMED_SINCE: a qualifying relationship exists now that did not exist at assessment - the claim keeps its historical state and displays this alongside it. UNREVIEWED: not re-checked since assessment, which is an honest default and not a synonym for UNCHANGED.

current_status_as_of.description: When current_status was last determined. Required so that UNCHANGED cannot silently age into a claim nobody has verified for years.

relationship_note.description: Required when current_status is RELATIONSHIP_FORMED_SINCE: what the relationship is, in plain words. A status with no description is not a disclosure.

otcs_version.description: The vocabulary version this record was written under. VERSIONING.md section 4 says a record means what its coordinates meant under the otcs_version it declares, and a later vocabulary never reaches back. That rule was unenforceable for claims until this field existed: only the project manifest carried a version, so a claim had no way to declare which dictionary governed it. Found by running an external reviewer's break test against the live schema.

depends_on.description: What this claim rests on, declared by identifier, version, and basis hash — the shape in-toto and SLSA use for the same problem (research/vocabulary-adoption, and the external reviewer's principle: every governed object declares its authoritative dependencies by identifier, version, and basis hash). Optional and additive: a claim without it validates exactly as before. The point of declaring is that standing can then read the declaration — a superseded or retracted dependency has somewhere to be recorded, and a recompute can see it. Without a declaration, a claim resting on an artifact superseded elsewhere reads as current forever, which was the one break of five the corpus could not catch.

identifier.description: The artifact this claim rests on — a URL, URN, or other stable name a stranger can resolve or recognise.

version.description: The exact version relied on. 'Latest' is not a version; the claim rested on something specific.

basis_hash.description: sha256 of the artifact as relied upon. The hash is what makes 'the same artifact' checkable rather than asserted.

status.description: Where the dependency stands now. CURRENT: re-checked, still the governing version. SUPERSEDED: a successor exists — the claim's standing decays until re-reviewed against it. RETRACTED: the artifact was withdrawn by its owner. UNREVIEWED: never re-checked since declaration, which is an honest default and not a synonym for CURRENT. Updating this field is a new fact about the world, not an edit to history — the declaration itself never changes.

status_as_of.description: When status was last determined. Required alongside CURRENT so that 'still current' cannot silently age into a claim nobody has verified for years.

superseded_by.description: The successor's identifier, when known. Lets a re-review start from the right place.

allOf.$comment: CURRENT is a positive assertion someone checked. It requires its date, or it is UNREVIEWED wearing a better label.

INDEPENDENTLY_TESTED is the strongest state this model can express and the one most worth inflating. It may not be claimed without saying who evaluated, when independence was assessed, and where that independence stands today.
States above DOCUMENTED assert that something outside the claim itself supports it. That assertion requires at least one evidence pointer.
